Style

Contemporary architecture

1207 buildings

Contemporary architecture is the architecture of the 21st century, from 2000 to today, and no single style leads it. It is shaped by method more than style: new structural systems make buildings taller, lighter and stronger than in the 20th century, and designs are modelled in 3D on computers. Some designers favour natural, ecological materials such as stone, wood and lime; energy efficiency over a building's whole life is a primary goal of sustainable design. The field is global, with important new buildings in China, Russia and India.

Read moreShow less

The Burj Khalifa in Dubai (2010), once the tallest building in the world, rises on a Y-shaped buttressed core that steps back in a spiral against the wind. Shigeru Ban's Centre Pompidou-Metz (2010) covers three stacked gallery tubes with a woven grid of glued laminated timber. Snøhetta's Oslo Opera House (2008) slopes a marble roof into the fjord, open for anyone to walk on. OMA's CCTV Headquarters in Beijing (2012) joins two leaning towers with a 75-metre cantilever. Herzog & de Meuron's Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg (2017) sets a glass crown on a brick warehouse, with a public plaza between old and new.

Questions students ask

What is contemporary architecture?

Contemporary architecture is what has been built in the 21st century, since 2000, with no one style in the lead. Method shapes it more than style does, and it spans the globe: major new work has gone up in China, Russia and India as well as in Europe and the Americas. Two examples are the Oslo Opera House by Snøhetta (2008) and the CCTV Headquarters in Beijing by OMA (2012).

What are the features of contemporary architecture?

Current structural systems let buildings be taller, lighter and stronger than twentieth-century ones, and projects are designed as 3D computer models. Some architects prefer natural, ecological materials, and sustainable design treats energy efficiency across a building's whole life as a main aim. The Centre Pompidou-Metz by Shigeru Ban, for instance, roofs its galleries with a woven lattice of glued laminated timber.

Which contemporary buildings should architecture students study?

Useful first examples: Toyo Ito's Sendai Mediatheque (2001), where thin floors rest on thirteen lattice tubes; OMA's Seattle Central Library (2004), whose book spiral is a single continuous ramp; Tate Modern in London (2000), a former power station now used as a museum; the Oslo Opera House (2008); and the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg (2017) by Herzog & de Meuron, which puts a glass crown on top of a brick warehouse.

Where can I see contemporary architecture?

Almost anywhere, because the field is global. In Asia and the Middle East there are the CCTV Headquarters in Beijing, the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, once the tallest building in the world, and Foster + Partners' Queen Alia International Airport in Amman. In Europe, see Casa da Música in Porto or the Markthal in Rotterdam; in North America, the High Line in New York.
